title: Robust automation: safe apply, rollforward and rollback protocol for Optimize recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket designs and implements API and SDK primitives plus webhook semantics to safely apply, rollforward, and rollback Optimize's batching/caching recommendations in automated flows. The goal is an idempotent, observable apply protocol that tolerates retries, partial failures, and operator-initiated rollbacks while minimizing customer risk and surprise cost regressions.

Context & goals:
- Optimize produces recommendations (batch sizes, cache policies, quantization tiers) and sends automation suggestions to customer accounts. We need a server-side API and webhook process so customers or Redwood automation agents can apply those changes safely.
- Requirements: idempotent apply operations, deterministic rollforward semantics for multi-step recommendations, authoritative rollback that reverts only what was changed by a specific apply, strong audit trail (who/what/when), and graceful handling of duplicate/parallel requests.
- This must integrate with the existing Optimize control plane and the SDKs used by Dedicated/Private agents.

Scope:
- New endpoints: /v1/optimize/apply, /v1/optimize/apply/status, /v1/optimize/rollback, /v1/optimize/webhook/ack (and DLQ hooks).
- Webhook payload spec and signature verification.
- Idempotency token mechanics, server-side dedup table, and TTL/compaction policy.
- Two-phase apply option for high-impact changes (plan -> approve -> commit) and a single-call apply for low-risk suggestions.
- Rollforward strategy to safely pick up partially-applied multi-resource plans.
- SDK helpers for JS/Python to generate idempotency tokens, observe state, and handle retries.

Non-goals:
- Full UI/Console rollout (handled in a follow-up).
- On-prem agent installer changes; we will provide API and SDK hooks for agent teams to adopt.

Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/infr/optimize/apply-protocol (WIP)
- Spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1728 (draft)
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after on-call incident where an apply retry caused duplicated batch-size increase for a customer. Key learning: missing idempotency and weak audit keys.
2026-02-18 Marco Rivera: Spiked server-side dedup store options (Redis vs MySQL ledger). Preliminary conclusion: use Redis for fast de-dup with fallback durable ledger in Postgres for reconciliation.
2026-02-25 Design review (Sofia Li): Requested explicit 'changed_by' and 'source' fields in apply records and a human-readable plan summary to show in rollbacks.
2026-03-03 Engineering review: Chose a bounded dedup TTL of 7 days with compaction job to archive older apply records to Postgres; added DLQ for failed webhooks after 5 retries.
2026-03-10 Marco Rivera: Implemented /v1/optimize/apply and basic idempotency store; integration tests added for duplicate apply retries. Planning rollout to staging tomorrow.
acceptance_criteria: Apply API accepts an idempotency_token and returns 202 + operation_id for async applies
Repeated POSTs with same idempotency_token must be deduplicated and return the same operation_id and final result
A failed apply that partially succeeded must record an atomic manifest describing applied resources and be rollable via operation_id
Rollback endpoint reverts only the resources listed in the manifest created by the original apply operation
Webhook consumer must verify signature and acknowledge events; Redwood retries deliver with exponential backoff and sends to DLQ after 5 failed attempts
SDKs provide helpers to generate RFC-4122 v4 idempotency tokens and to poll apply status, with example code in JS and Python
Observability: each apply/rollback emits trace/span with operation_id, cost impact estimate, and token.owner metadata
tasks: Design API surface: request/response schemas, headers, HTTP codes
Implement idempotency store: Redis dedup + Postgres ledger + compaction job
Implement apply planner that emits a step manifest and deterministic resource ids
Implement rollback engine that consumes a manifest and performs compensating ops
Add webhook delivery path and DLQ with signature verification and ack semantics
Add SDK helpers and integration test matrix (duplicate retries, network partitions, concurrent applies)
Run chaos tests: simulate partial failures, double-apply, and mid-apply server restarts
Create runbook for on-call: detecting duplicate-applies and invoking manual rollbacks
implementation_notes: Idempotency token model: X-Idempotency-Token header, RFC-4122 v4 recommended. Server stores token -> operation_id mapping with TTL and final outcome.
Dedup store behavior: write-once semantics. First writer wins; subsequent writers read outcome. Use Redis SETNX with operation metadata blob pointer to Postgres record.
Manifest format: newline-delimited JSON strings in Postgres for compact audit; manifest includes resource_type, resource_id, previous_config_hash, applied_config_hash, and timestamp.
Two-phase apply: for high-impact recs (cost delta > threshold) we return proposed_plan and require explicit commit with same idempotency_token to proceed. Low-risk applies can be auto-committed.
Rollback guarantees: best-effort idempotent compensating operations. If a compensating operation fails, the rollback reports partial revert and surfaces items to DLQ for manual remediation.
Observability: attach operation_id to logs, traces, and billing delta estimates. Emit metrics: optimize.apply.attempts, optimize.apply.duplicates, optimize.apply.rollback.counts.
Security: webhook signatures use HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer secret stored in KMS; signatures verified per delivery and included in audit record.
webhook_spec: Event types: optimize.recommendation.created, optimize.recommendation.apply.started, optimize.recommendation.apply.completed, optimize.recommendation.apply.failed, optimize.recommendation.rollback.completed
Delivery: POST JSON to registered endpoint with X-Redwood-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256). Body includes event_id, operation_id, recommendation_id, timestamp, and human_summary.
Ack: 2xx = success; non-2xx triggers retry with exponential backoff. After 5 failed attempts send event to DLQ and mark delivery_failed in audit record.
Replay: events contain reproducible event_id and operation_id for safe replay by idempotency checks on consumer side.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotency store: verify dedup for same token across multiple concurrent requests
Integration tests for end-to-end apply + rollback with staged chaos (network flaps, partial service kill)
Contract tests for webhook signature verification and ack/retry behavior
Load test for dedup store under burst of 5k apply requests/sec across multiple customers
Manual verification run against staging with a seeded customer to validate cost delta telemetry and rollback fidelity
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: token reuse by different actors could accidentally deduplicate unrelated requests. Mitigation: bind idempotency_token scope to (customer_id, token) and include 'actor' in the dedup key.
Risk: long TTL dedup state may prevent legitimate replays after legitimate config drift. Mitigation: TTL default 7d with admin override to forget tokens and an archival path to resume reconciliation.
Risk: partial rollback leaving resources in an inconsistent state. Mitigation: manifest driven rollback with per-resource retry and DLQ for manual recovery.
